entries.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Production final death key pose for a 2D game animation. Attached image is the approved original DESIGN AND SCALE AUTHORITY, not a rejected animation. Redraw exactly ONE complete cotton-sheep in the following new pose: The sheep has collapsed onto its left side after its knees gave way. Draw a genuinely NEW limp body configuration: the same round woolly torso has rolled 20 degrees toward the viewer, with its side and chest on the ground; bent forelegs lie forward in front of the chest with recognizable cream shins and brown hooves, bent rear hocks and hooves remain visible alongside the rear belly. The cheek and small pink-brown nose rest close to the forelegs on that same ground, head tilted only moderately, both ears flop softly. Fully closed eyes, inert ears and tail. Do not simply rotate the standing animal or detach its head; change leg articulation, overlaps and visible belly surfaces for a believable collapse. Keep the precise original oversized wool forehead clump arrangement, cream face shape, large floppy ears, fluffy short tail, round wool clusters and head/torso proportions. No extra collar or long neck. Keep the original polished painted cartoon style, thin colored-dark contour, lighting, palette, recognizable pattern details, unchanged anatomical proportions and three-quarter camera. The pose may change occlusions and expose hidden surfaces, but the same skull, torso, limb lengths, ears, feathers and wool clusters must be identifiable. Fixed square canvas with generous transparent margins, same character physical scale as the reference. Feet/body/cheek contact one horizontal floor around 85% down the canvas. Genuine transparent alpha background. No floor artwork, cast shadow, debris, particles, effects, text, labels, grid, multiple characters, gore or animation sheet. This drawing will become actual production key-pose and part source.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Production MIDDLE COLLAPSE KEY for a 2D game death animation. Image 1 is the approved upright original design and physical-scale authority. Image 2 is the selected final death drawing, ONLY to establish the destination pose. Draw exactly ONE complete intermediate pose, no sheet: The foreknees have just buckled onto the floor; hips and hindlegs are still partly raised. The round torso tips down toward the lowered chest, its anatomical volume and original wool clusters unchanged. Fore shins and hooves slide a little forward with elbows bent; hind hocks begin folding. The head is following the chest downward with eyes narrowing but the cheek has not yet contacted the floor. Both ears are lagging behind the head, same original width and length, not fused into the wool. All four short legs remain connected and identifiable. This is about halfway through the collapse, before the final side rest. Match image 1 exactly in head dimensions, torso volume/length, limb and ear lengths, distinctive surface markings/wool clusters/feather patterns, style, lighting and palette. Keep the same three-quarter camera. Match image 2's final identity without prematurely reaching that final pose. Do not enlarge the head or flatten the torso. Fixed square canvas, generous transparent margins, same physical scale as the images, same horizontal ground plane. True transparent RGBA alpha. No floor or cast-shadow drawing, no effects, particles, gore, text, labels, grid, multiple characters or motion trails. This key will be used as an actual anatomy/occlusion source for local rig intervals and transitions.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Actual production layered anatomical source kit for a hybrid 2D death animation. Image1 is the APPROVED ORIGINAL design authority; image2 is the new final-collapse key for joint/overlap guidance. Nine separate parts in a 3 by 3 atlas: row1 complete fluffy torso WITHOUT head, ears, legs or tail; complete original head INCLUDING the exact original oversized wool forehead clusters and cream face, eyes open, WITHOUT ears or chest/neck wool collar; full near floppy ear. Row2 full far floppy ear; complete near foreleg from soft wool shoulder root through cream elbow/shin to brown hoof; complete far foreleg, same anatomy. Row3 complete near hindleg from soft wool hip root through bent knee/hock to brown hoof; complete far hindleg; short fluffy tail. The four legs must be continuous complete limbs, softly bent standing reference anatomy with hidden upper roots drawn, clear knee and ankle positions, solid coherent skin and hoof, no limb chopped into pieces. Keep the sheep's short original leg lengths and original round torso volume. Every attachment is individually complete, continuous, independently separated by generous transparent space, hidden contours fully painted with natural rounded fur/feather/wool, no stump cross sections, flat sliced planes, holes or outlined socket circles. Preserve exact design/texture motifs, palette, line weight, original anatomical proportions and three-quarter view. Parts are in neutral orientation for one-time anatomical registration; no animation frames. All parts should be large enough for clean extraction and full detail. True transparent RGBA alpha. No gray/white backgrounds, checkerboards, shadows, labels, text, borders, frames, grid lines, arrows, extra parts or assembled characters.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Exact production expression attachment edit. Edit ONLY the eyes of this isolated cotton-sheep head to fully closed relaxed eyelids. Preserve every other pixel and silhouette: identical skull size and shape, same wool clumps/feather spots/fur markings, same nose, beak, forehead, cheek volume and colors. Keep the head in exactly the same position and orientation on the same square transparent canvas with the same margins. No ears, horns, torso, neck, added collars or other objects. Do not recenter, zoom, resize, rotate or redraw the head design. True transparent alpha background. This actual alternate eye artwork will be precisely registered and composited into the locked head attachment, keeping the original geometry.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Draw ONE actual bridge CEL for the SAME cotton-sheep death animation, not a concept variation. Image1 is the approved standing original and exact anatomy/style authority; image2 is the selected middle knee-collapse key; image3 is the selected final rest key. Target temporal pose: Between the kneeling image2 and the final image3, about 60% toward image3: front knees and hooves already contact ground, chest and cheek just meet the forelegs at the floor. Rear hocks finish folding, pelvis is lowering but has not completely settled. The same exact head, ears and forehead wool clusters from image2 retain their size and shape, now with eyes fully closed. Ears lag behind the head by a few degrees. Whole creature remains connected, rear hooves plainly identifiable. This is the contact before the final relaxed side-rest in image3. Maintain precisely the same physical scale of the skull, wool forehead clumps, face, torso mass, ear lengths and all four short legs across these adjacent poses. No larger head, no new wool clumps, no thinner/thicker torso or changed markings. Same lighting, palette, thin contour, painted cartoon style and three-quarter camera. One square transparent canvas with a fixed ground plane and generous margins. Contact feet share the same floor. Only articulation, body position, overlap and legitimate perspective change. No floor artwork, shadows, text, grid, duplicated characters, effects or gore. This cel will be placed directly into the production sequence between its neighbor poses.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Actual production layered BODY POSE source atlas for this SAME cotton-sheep death action, with its head rendered on a separate locked attachment. Image1 approved original design. Image2 selected middle kneeling pose. Image3 selected final rest. Create SIX HEADLESS BODY POSES, arranged cleanly as a 3-column by 2-row atlas, chronological row-major order. In EVERY pose remove the ENTIRE skull, cream face, nose, forehead wool crown and BOTH ears. Complete the soft wool forechest and neck base underneath that removed head as a natural continuous connected wool body, so a separate head can overlap it. Do not leave a flat cut, neck hole, empty socket, hard straight line, scarf or an extra head-shaped wool ball. Keep the original round torso volume, short cream leg lengths, brown hoof sizes, fluffy tail, exact pale wool colors and distinctive wool clump arrangement. Each body is a connected anatomical body+four legs+tail, all hidden limb roots drawn. SAME exact physical unit scale and same 3/4 camera in all six cells, same ground line within each cell, generous clear gutters. 1: standing original body with straight short legs, stable support. 2: foreknees start buckling, forehooves slide slightly forward, chest drops a little; pelvis still high. 3: both foreknees contact the floor and forehooves lie forward, chest lowering, hindfeet still planted/high pelvis. 4: forechest rests low and rear hocks fold, pelvis lowering, intact four hooves visible. 5: full torso/flank rests on ground, bent forelegs/paws forward and bent hind hocks beside belly, soft wool forechest clearly supports a separately overlaid cheek. 6: same final body contact with rear hooves finishing a small relaxed settling movement, body mass/headless chest shape unchanged from5. Preserve size and pattern continuity; do not enlarge, shrink, flatten, stretch or change the torso design from cell to cell. Genuine transparent alpha background. No heads, eyes, ears, face features, text, labels, grid lines, borders, shadows, loose pieces, duplicate legs or effects. These are actual production body cels, not a planning illustration.
